section_1.title: The Core Concept: Defining Populations
section_1.content: Introduce the three compartmental states: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R). Explain the total population constraint (N = S + I + R) and the concept of 'flow' between states.
section_1.example: Visualize a group of 100 forest rabbits. Blue (S) are healthy, Red (I) are sick, and Green (R) have developed immunity.

section_2.title: The Dynamics of Transmission (The Math of Interaction)
section_2.content: Explain the transition rates. Focus on the transmission rate (beta) as the likelihood of infection during contact. Use a graphic representing 'Blue' colliding with 'Red' to become 'Red'.
section_2.example: An animation showing a 'Red' rabbit hopping through a field; every time it bumps into a 'Blue' rabbit, there is a probability that the 'Blue' rabbit turns 'Red'.

section_3.title: The Recovery Mechanism (The Gamma Factor)
section_3.content: Introduce the removal rate (gamma), representing the time it takes for an infected individual to stop being infectious (recovery or death). Explain how I decreases while R increases.
section_3.example: A timer icon appearing over 'Red' rabbits. Once the timer ends, they shift color to Green, signifying they can no longer infect or be infected.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Curves
section_4.content: Synthesize the logic into the classic SIR line graph. Discuss the peak of the 'I' curve and what it represents (the epidemic peak). Explain why the 'S' curve always declines and the 'R' curve always rises.
section_4.example: An animated line chart evolving in real-time alongside the rabbit simulation: watch the Red curve spike as the forest gets infected and flatten as herd immunity (the Green population) grows.

section_5.title: Application: The Power of Intervention
section_5.content: Briefly demonstrate how changing variables (e.g., social distancing reducing beta) shifts the curves. Conclude with why mathematical modeling is crucial for public health policy.
section_5.example: Show a 'Fence' barrier appearing in the forest animation, reducing the collision frequency between rabbits, resulting in a 'flattened' Red curve on the graph.
